sentences.text:
Neetu @ Nitin Rathore vs State Of Uttarakhand on 10 December,
2024
Author: Ravindra Maithani

Bench: Ravindra Maithani
High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 First Bail Application No.2626 of 2023
Neetu @ Nitin Rathore ........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Present:-

Mr. Rishabh Bisht, Advocate holding brief of Mr. Vikas
 Kumar Guglani, Advocate for the applicant.
Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, Dag for the State.
Mr. Digvijay Singh Bisht, Advocate for the informant.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)

Applicant is in judicial custody in First Information Report No.10 of 2023, under Sections 498A,
376, 313 Ipc and Section 5/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012, Police
Station Dharchula, District Pithoragarh, Uttarakhand.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: He has sought his release on bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
According to the prosecution case, the victim and the applicant, both were married.
Prior to marriage, when the victim was a child, the applicant had established physical relations with her.
After marriage, the victim was harassed and tortured in connection with demand of dowry.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that parties are married.
The victim is the wife of the applicant.
He would submit that the victim is major.
5. Learned counsel for the informant would submit that the victim has supported the prosecution case during trial.
6. State adopts the arguments, as advanced by the learned counsel for the informant.
7. Having considered, this Court is of the view that it is a case fit for bail and the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
8. The bail application is allowed.
